- [decision] Failed-payment retry schedule (id: 01a1080c-b451-7f52-a956-ad3f60f2f6db; source: shared/human)
  When a charge fails, retry it on days 1, 3, 7, 14 after the failure (contractual, finance policy FP-12). If the day-14 retry also fails, mark the invoice `uncollectible` and stop. Never retry an invoice that has a refund in progress.

  Every new operation that moves money (refund, credit, write-off) logs an audit event through structlog named `ledger.<noun>_<past-tense verb>`, for example `ledger.refund_issued` or `ledger.credit_applied`, and the event must include `actor_id` (the user or service that triggered it). from dataclasses import dataclass, field

import requests
import structlog

log = structlog.get_logger()

LEDGER_URL = "https://ledger.internal.acme.example/v1/postings"


@dataclass
class Invoice:
    id: str
    customer_id: str
    subtotal_cents: int
    tax_cents: int = 0
    ledger_ref: str | None = None
    lines: list = field(default_factory=list)


def finalize(invoice):
    resp = requests.post(LEDGER_URL, json={"invoice": invoice.id, "amount": invoice.subtotal_cents + invoice.tax_cents}, timeout=10)
    resp.raise_for_status()
    invoice.ledger_ref = resp.json()["ref"]
    log.info("invoice_finalized", invoice_id=invoice.id)
    return invoice


def finalize_once(invoice):
    if invoice.ledger_ref:
        return invoice
    return finalize(invoice)
import pytest
import requests

SANDBOX = "https://sandbox.payments.example/v1/charges"


@pytest.mark.integration
def test_charges_roundtrip():
    for amount in (100, 250, 999, 1200):
        resp = requests.post(SANDBOX, json={"amount_cents": amount}, timeout=10)
        assert resp.status_code == 201

input.summary: CI runs pytest with -W error: any warning (e.g. DeprecationWarning) fails the build
input.content: CI runs pytest with `-W error`, so any warning raised during tests — notably DeprecationWarning — becomes an error and fails the build, even though the same tests pass locally (`make test-fast` does not pass -W error). This flag lives in the CI config, not in pyproject.toml or the Makefile. Before pushing new tests or code, run them locally with `python -m pytest -W error ...` and avoid deprecated APIs.

I also saved this to the project memory so it comes up in later sessions and for other people working here. That entry also notes two things:
